finalText:
All ten requirements come from section 3.1.1.2 (Password Verifiers) of NIST SP 800-63B-4, which is the current revision.

**Which revision is current.** The CSRC publication page (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) returned a 404 error, so I confirmed the revision another way. The Rev 3 page (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) says: "This revision of NIST SP 800-63 has been superseded by NIST SP 800-63-4 as of August 1, 2025." The Rev 4 HTML page (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html) is dated Tue, 26 Aug 2025. Its abstract says it "supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." I found no newer revision, errata box or withdrawal notice. All quotes below come from that one Rev 4 page.

**Requirements (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html):**
- **Minimum length when a password is the only factor:** 15 characters (SHALL). This is up from Rev 3's 8-character minimum. Passwords used only within multi-factor authentication MAY be shorter, but SHALL still be at least 8 characters.
- **Maximum length:** verifiers SHOULD permit a maximum length of at least 64 characters.
- **Composition rules** (such as requiring a mix of character types): SHALL NOT be imposed. Section 3.1.1.1 says the same.
- **Periodic change:** verifiers SHALL NOT require it. They SHALL force a change if there is evidence the password has been compromised.
- **Password hints** that unauthenticated claimants can see: SHALL NOT be permitted.
- **Knowledge-based authentication or security questions** when a password is chosen: SHALL NOT be prompted.
- **Blocklist:** verifiers SHALL check new and changed passwords against a list of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords.
- **Password managers and autofill:** verifiers SHALL allow them. Verifiers SHOULD also allow pasting.
- **Salt length:** SHALL be at least 32 bits.
- **Hashing scheme:** an approved scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132 (or later NIST guidance) SHOULD be used. This is only a SHOULD. The firm requirement is that passwords "SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme."
